newsitem.title: INDIA: India EIH first half holds no surprises.
newsitem.headline: India EIH first half holds no surprises.

text.p: Lower hotel occupancies hit first half profits of leading Indian hospitality firm EIH Ltd in the six months to September 30, 1996, but results met most market expectations, analysts said on Wednesday.
"Absolutely on line. There were no surprises," said Anamica Gawri, analyst at securities firm Peregrine Capital.
EIH -- formerly East India Hotels -- said on Wednesday its net rose 18.87 percent to 474.3 million in the first half of fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) from 399 million a year ago.
EIH said the first half results were not indicative of its full year working.
"The first half was basically election time and the lower occupancies are a fallout of how the elections impacted business travel," said a hotel analyst at a European brokerage.
National elections -- spread over April and May -- resulted in the formation of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's 13-party ruling coalition United Front.
Hotel occupanies, which traditionally drop during election time, were slow to pick up due to political worries.
Analyst Priya Uppal at Jardine Fleming India Broking said occupancy was 65 percent in the first half of the current year, a fall of four percent from the year ago.
She said the average room rate (ARR) during the period had gone up by 36 percent to 6,400 rupees from 4,700.
"In Delhi, the firm did reasonably well. It had an advantage over Indian Hotels as some of their rooms were under renovation," said Sowmya Vencatesan, at ICICI Securities.
Indian Hotels Company is the flagship of the country's biggest hotel chain -- the Taj Group of Hotels.
Both firms draw more than 70 percent of their revenues from hotels in the major cities of Bombay, New Delhi and Calcutta.
Analyts said the second half would see sharply improved results. They forecast a full year net profit in the range of 1,510 million rupees to 1,530 million.
Analysts said EIH's stock could see some price contraction as some fund managers had expected the firm to perform better in the first six months.
EIH's share closed 4.50 rupees lower at 359.25 rupees on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE).
